races.title: State Senate, District 11
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Lisa Stone Barnes
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 11 (Franklin, Nash and Vance counties) since 2021. Previously served in the NC House (District 7, 2019-2021) and six years on the Nash County Board of Commissioners. Career as a real estate paralegal and in agribusiness.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Her campaign site says only that she has worked to keep taxes low and supports responsible spending, quality education and healthcare. We found no records of bills she sponsored, because the sponsored-legislation list on her Ballotpedia page was empty. We found no endorsements for the 2026 race, and she did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. The pages did not say when or whether she lived anywhere other than Nash County.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born in Nash County and graduated from Southern Nash High School, and her campaign site calls her a Nash County native who has lived and served there for decades.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC Senate since 2021 and the NC House 2019-2021, after six years as a Nash County commissioner. Worked as a real estate paralegal, in the Rocky Mount Planning and Development Department, and in agribusiness.
qual.why: Roughly seven years of prior legislative service plus local elected office and a paralegal and planning career fit the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: Roughly seven years of prior legislative service plus local elected office and a paralegal and planning career fit the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chair posts were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In her 2012 campaign for Nash County commissioner she opposed a proposed Sanderson Farms poultry processing plant, citing environmental concerns she had raised while on the county planning board.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Wikipedia says she was born in Nash County and graduated from Southern Nash High School, and her campaign site calls her a Nash County native who has lived and served there for decades.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Opposed the proposed Sanderson Farms poultry processing plant in Nash County, citing environmental concerns she had raised on the county planning board. She challenged the incumbent commissioner, who supported the plant, and won.

cands.name: James D. Gailliard
cands.bio: Senior pastor of Word Tabernacle Church in Rocky Mount and founder of The REACH Center. Democrat. Served in the North Carolina House (District 25) from 2019 to 2023. Won the District 11 state Senate seat on Nov. 3, 2026, defeating incumbent Lisa Barnes.

endorsements.text: Senate Minority Leader Sydney Batch is quoted on his campaign site endorsing him for the N.C. Senate.
Former U.S. Rep. G.K. Butterfield is quoted on his campaign site endorsing him for the N.C. Senate.

cands.gaps: We could not find where James Gailliard was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. The pages we had list no bills he sponsored and give no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying by out-of-state or foreign investors, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site names priorities such as Medicaid expansion, down payment assistance, broadband and criminal justice reform, but these do not map to specific actions. No news reporting on controversies or documented foreign ties was available. His campaign site is a promotional source and was used only for what he and his supporters say.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign says he has been the organizing senior pastor of Word Tabernacle Church in Rocky Mount for over 25 years, and a supporter's endorsement refers to his arrival in Nash County, so the record shows 25+ years of adult life in North Carolina; his birthplace and upbringing are not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served two terms in the NC House (2019-2023) and has been senior pastor of Word Tabernacle Church for over 25 years. His campaign also lists him as founder and chairman of The REACH Center, Inc.
qual.why: Prior legislative service puts him in the high range. His long record of running a large church and community organization adds management experience. Committee seats and board roles were not counted.
qual.label: Prior legislative service puts him in the high range. His long record of running a large church and community organization adds management experience. Committee seats and board roles were not counted.
